Module 03 · Prompts

Library: direct co-creation

Choose a task, observe your practice, compare sources, co-create the Mini-SOP, and test one case under human review.

View promptsPlaybook
Where to run each prompt

Two interfaces. One clear workflow.

Use Chat to work with sources already in the notebook. Use Sources to find and import new material.

Ask, audit, practise or create

Select the relevant sources and paste the prompt into Chat. NotebookLM answers from that selection and shows citations for review.

How it works in NotebookLM
Find and import evidence

Paste the research question into Sources. Use Fast Research for a quick search or Deep Research for a full briefing. Review results before importing them.

How it works in NotebookLM

You may start in Chat to refine the question. To find and add new sources, finish the step in Sources and then return to Chat.

Open NotebookLM4 · Prompt structure levels

Why it worksAcceptance criteria
Purpose
Bound a useful workflow.
When to use it
When starting from a task or workflow that is not yet bounded.
Trade-off
Less scope gives more control.
Next
Diagnose friction

Workflow

  • Define purpose and outcome.
  • Bound start, finish, and risk.
  • State decision and stop.

Best practices and frameworks

  • Light SIPOC
  • Definition of Done

Guardrails

  • Do not invent my context.
  • Keep the final decision human and request any missing input.

Acceptance criteria

  • Has scope and owner.
  • A case exists.
  • Boundary is written.

Edge cases

  • If no case exists, state that evidence is absent.

Limits

  • Does not execute.

N1Direct

A clear, concise instruction.

Objective: Bound a useful workflow. Inputs 1

Parameters

  • STRUCTURE = short table + decision
  • DEPTH = operational

Why it worksAcceptance criteria
Purpose
Diagnose friction.
When to use it
When you have the artifact from prompt 01.
Trade-off
Prudence reduces apparent certainty.
Next
Find relevant practices

Workflow

  • Reconstruct the case.
  • Mark friction.
  • Separate facts and hypotheses.

Best practices and frameworks

  • Friction map
  • Five Whys as questions

Guardrails

  • Do not assign causes.
  • Keep the final decision human and request any missing input.

Acceptance criteria

  • Every friction has a moment.
  • Causes remain labeled.
  • Observation is separate from hypothesis.

Edge cases

  • If frictions compete, prioritize by impact and testability.

Limits

  • Does not claim causality.

Why it worksAcceptance criteria
Purpose
Find relevant practices.
When to use it
When you have the artifact from prompt 02.
Trade-off

Next
Map the current process

Workflow

  • Ask from friction.
  • Extract source and condition.
  • Adapt, test, or reject.

Best practices and frameworks

  • Evidence matrix
  • Context comparison

Guardrails

  • Use identifiable sources.
  • Keep the final decision human and request any missing input.

Acceptance criteria

  • Retains provenance.
  • Explains differences.
  • Sources are accessible.

Edge cases

  • If no case exists, state that evidence is absent.

Limits

  • Does not universalize recipes.

Workflow

  • Order inputs and outputs.
  • Assign decisions.

Best practices and frameworks

  • Light SIPOC
  • Minimal blueprint

Guardrails

  • Do not complete missing facts.
  • Keep the final decision human and request any missing input.

Acceptance criteria

  • Separates current and future.
  • Every decision has owner.
  • Decisions are explicit.

Edge cases

  • If frictions compete, prioritize by impact and testability.

Limits

  • Does not design future.

  • Assign prevention and response.

  • Pre-mortem
  • Risk register

Guardrails

  • Do not present risks as events.
  • Keep the final decision human and request any missing input.

Acceptance criteria

  • Every risk has signal.
  • Decisions remain human.
  • Risks have responses.

  • Does not quantify without data.

Why it worksAcceptance criteria
Purpose
Design a controlled test.
When to use it
When you have the artifact from prompt 07.
Trade-off

Next

Workflow

  • Set case and criteria.
  • Retain inputs.
  • Define log and reviewer.

Best practices and frameworks

  • PDCA
  • PASA

Guardrails

  • Do not execute the plan.
  • Keep the final decision human and request any missing input.

Acceptance criteria

  • Can stop safely.
  • Reconstructs the case.
  • Case is reversible.

Edge cases

  • If frictions compete, prioritize by impact and testability.

Limits

  • Does not execute or approve.

Workflow

  • Compare expectation and result.
  • Separate failure and exception.
  • Submit changes to decision.

Best practices and frameworks

  • AAR
  • Decision log

Guardrails

  • Do not hide failures.
  • Keep the final decision human and request any missing input.

Acceptance criteria

  • Conclusions cite records.
  • Changes receive decisions.
  • Conclusions link to log.

Edge cases

  • If no case exists, state that evidence is absent.

Limits

  • Does not invent evidence.

For your practice

Turn one real task into a way of working you can repeat.

When every delivery depends on memory and improvisation, you repeat decisions, carry friction, and cannot tell what AI improved.

What you will gain

You will leave with a clear personal workflow, a test log, and a version you can reuse without losing control.

How to proceed

Choose a task, observe your practice, compare sources, co-create the Mini-SOP, and test one case under human review.

What to verify

A Mini-SOP with input, steps, criteria, human review, output, exceptions, and a real-case test log.

Design my workflow

Repeat the workflow on a second case and change only what the log supports.
